body:
WHAT
Two things must be true of the Windows build, and both are proved on the artifact itself, not on the config alone. BUILD: `npm run dist` (app/) bundles the engine with rg.exe and runs electron-builder, producing MAGENTRA-<version>-win-portable.exe, MAGENTRA-<version>-win-setup.exe (NSIS, non-one-click, directory choosable), latest.yml, and an unpacked app in app/dist/win-unpacked/ containing MAGENTRA.exe, magentra-cli.exe (console-subsystem copy) and resources/engine/{engine.cjs, doc-extract.mjs, tui.mjs, rg.exe}. READINESS: the built app opens for a standard, NON-ADMIN Windows user with no UAC prompt — both exes carry an `asInvoker` execution level in their embedded manifest — and `MAGENTRA.exe --smoke --user-data-dir=<tmp>` boots Electron, loads the renderer, and exits 0 within 60 s (main.js exits 1 if the renderer process dies). The bundled Grep binary runs (`resources\engine\rg.exe --version` exits 0). The engine bundle boots as Node (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 MAGENTRA.exe resources\engine\engine.cjs --bogus` prints the host's fatal `error` frame and exits 1 — proving engine.cjs is loadable without node_modules). CROSS-OS: this test runs only where the artifact can be produced and launched — process.platform === 'win32'. On any other OS it fails loudly with 'Windows artifact tests need a Windows machine; the release workflow's windows leg is the proof there', and the workflow assertion (item 6) demands that leg smoke-launches the packaged app.

WHY
A config-only test proved the last build's argv, not that a user could open the result: a portable exe whose sandboxed children die at boot, an installer that demands admin rights, or a bundle missing rg.exe all pass a package.json check and fail on the first real machine. Non-admin is the case that matters: every corporate or shared PC user is one.

WHERE
app/package.json — scripts.dist, build.win.target ["portable","nsis"], build.win.extraResources filter [engine.cjs, doc-extract.mjs, tui.mjs, rg.exe], build.portable.artifactName, build.nsis { artifactName, oneClick:false, allowToChangeInstallationDirectory:true, include build/installer.nsh }, no `perMachine` (so NSIS installs per-user and both exes are asInvoker). app/scripts/dist.js — spawnSync('electron-builder', ['--publish','never', ...argv, -c.electronVersion, -c.extraMetadata.magentraCommit]). app/scripts/bundle-engine.js — RIPGREP { target:'win', src: node_modules/@vscode/ripgrep-win32-x64/bin/rg.exe }, parseTargets(), the throw for a missing target rg. app/scripts/afterPack.js — writeConsoleSubsystemCopy() writing magentra-cli.exe beside MAGENTRA.exe. app/main.js — `const SMOKE = process.argv.includes("--smoke")` (line 42), the single-instance lock skipped under SMOKE (line 48), did-finish-load → `app.exit(rendererCrashed ? 1 : 0)` after 5 s, render-process-gone → the one-shot --no-sandbox relaunch and `if (SMOKE) app.exit(1)`. engine/host/src/main.ts — parseArgs() rejecting an unknown flag with a fatal error frame. .github/workflows/release.yml — the windows matrix leg (os windows-latest, `npm run dist:win`, upload app/dist/*.exe app/dist/latest.yml). tests/lib/procTest.ts — the kind these run under; tests/lib/exclusive.ts — withExclusiveLock, because the build writes shared output.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. BUILD (proc, win32 only, exclusive lock 'dist', timeout 15 min): run `npm run dist` in app/ with a clean app/dist; assert exit 0 and that app/dist contains exactly MAGENTRA-<package.json version>-win-portable.exe, MAGENTRA-<version>-win-setup.exe, its .blockmap and latest.yml (whose `version` equals package.json's and whose `path` names the setup exe), and that app/dist/win-unpacked/ holds MAGENTRA.exe, magentra-cli.exe and resources/engine/{engine.cjs, doc-extract.mjs, tui.mjs, rg.exe}. Every later item reuses this output and fails (never skips) with 'run item 1 first' when win-unpacked is absent.
2. NON-ADMIN READY (pure on the artifact): read the bytes of both MAGENTRA.exe and the setup exe and assert each contains the manifest text `requestedExecutionLevel level="asInvoker"` and neither contains `level="requireAdministrator"` or `level="highestAvailable"`; assert magentra-cli.exe differs from MAGENTRA.exe in exactly the two Subsystem bytes (value 3 vs 2 at e_lfanew+24+68) and is otherwise identical.
3. LAUNCHES (proc): spawn app/dist/win-unpacked/MAGENTRA.exe with ['--smoke', '--user-data-dir=<fresh temp dir>'] and a clean env (no MAGENTRA_* variables); assert it exits with code 0 within 60 s, that <temp>/ contains the app's own log with a 'landing-shown' event and no 'render-process-gone' event, and that no 'sandbox-rescue-relaunch' was needed. Then repeat with the portable exe (PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_DIR semantics are electron-builder's own; only exit 0 and the log are asserted) — this is the double-click path a non-admin user takes.
4. TOOLS READY (proc): run `resources\engine\rg.exe --version` from win-unpacked and assert exit 0 and stdout starting 'ripgrep'; run MAGENTRA.exe with env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and args ['resources/engine/engine.cjs', '--bogus'] and assert exit code 1 with a single stdout line parsing as `{type:'error', fatal:true}` — the engine bundle loads and runs without node_modules.
5. NAMES AGREE (pure): app/main/updates.js assetName for win32 nsis/portable equals the two file names produced in item 1 for this version; latest.yml's sha512 matches the setup exe's actual SHA-512 (base64) — the updater would accept this build.
6. CI IS THE OTHER OS (pure): .github/workflows/release.yml's windows leg runs `npm run dist:win` (or dist) AND a step that launches the packaged MAGENTRA.exe with `--smoke` and fails the job on a non-zero exit; the mac and linux legs have the same smoke step for their artifacts. Until those steps exist this item fails — that is the point: what cannot be launched on this machine is launched on the matching runner, never assumed.
